comparison: Both evaluations support claims C1-C3 regarding the CRISPR screen's success in identifying DNA repair factors. OpenEval additionally covers C4 (KEGG pathway enrichment). Both note the screen identified known and unknown repair factors, validating the methodology.

Both support the identification of METTL3/14 and WTAP through proteomics (C5, C17, C18). OpenEval additionally mentions C102 (functional cooperation). Peer review explicitly acknowledges the unexpected identification of RNA m6A methyltransferase METTL3 in DNA repair context.

Perfect alignment on claims C6-C11 regarding UNG2 foci formation and specificity for uracil-inducing agents. Both evaluations support the immunofluorescence data and specificity demonstrated by differential responses to DNA damaging agents.

Strong agreement on claims C12-C14, C16 regarding IDR characterization and condensate formation. OpenEval explicitly mentions all claims while peer review implicitly accepts by not challenging the optoDroplet and functional rescue data.
Both address C15 (functional rescue experiments). OpenEval groups this with IDR/condensate claims, while peer review treats it separately. Both support the data without challenge.

Perfect alignment on claims C19-C22 regarding METTL3 requirement through genetic and pharmacological approaches. Peer review notes the evidence is accepted but suggests rescue experiments with catalytic mutant would strengthen conclusions further.

Strong agreement on claims C23-C27, C47 regarding DNA localization through nuclease treatments. Both evaluations emphasize the elegance and conclusiveness of these experiments. Peer review explicitly calls evidence 'conclusive' while OpenEval notes this addresses a major field challenge.

Both support claims C28-C29, C48 regarding UPLC-MS/MS detection of 6mA in DNA. OpenEval additionally mentions C98. Both emphasize the orthogonal nature of mass spectrometry and its ability to definitively distinguish DNA from RNA.

Perfect alignment on claims C32-C33, C52, C101 regarding METTL3-dependence of 6mA foci formation. Both evaluations support the inhibition and knockout data establishing METTL3 as a writer of 6mA in this context.

Strong agreement on claims C34-C38 regarding epistasis experiments establishing pathway order. OpenEval additionally mentions C103. Both accept the mechanistic interpretation that 6mA acts upstream of UNG2 recruitment.
Perfect alignment on claim C39 regarding biolayer interferometry showing no direct effect of 6mA on UNG binding in purified system. Both accept this negative result and acknowledge its limitations.

Strong agreement on claims C40-C43 regarding expansion of METTL3/6mA function to other base-damaging agents beyond uracil. OpenEval additionally mentions C104. Both support the broader role established by these data.
Perfect alignment on claims C44-C45 regarding increased mutation frequency with METTL3 inhibition. Both evaluations support the functional link to genome stability and MMR function.

Both address contamination concerns (C50-C51). OpenEval groups these with damage-induced nature (C46, C49, C99) while peer review focuses specifically on contamination. Editor explicitly states evidence is convincing that signal does not result from bacterial contamination or RNA.

Partial overlap on C46, C99 (damage-induced nature, functional relevance). Peer review R15 broadly affirms novelty and significance of METTL3-6mA-UNG2 axis, while OpenEval R13 focuses on technical aspects addressing contamination concerns.

Both address literature-based contextual claims. OpenEval covers C30-C31, C53-C55 (prior work on METTL3/6mA), while peer review R16 covers broader set including C67, C86-C90. Both accept these as appropriate context without challenge.

Both address APEX2 proximity data (C63, C68) suggesting roles for RNA modification machinery in DNA repair. OpenEval notes lack of functional validation, while peer review groups with other discussion/speculation claims as appropriately framed future directions.

Strong agreement on claims C56-C57, C60 regarding therapeutic implications and future applications. Both evaluations note these are appropriately framed as speculative/hypothetical. OpenEval additionally mentions C61 and rates as UNCERTAIN, while peer review accepts as SUPPORTED speculation.

Both address claims C58-C59 regarding clinical context from literature. OpenEval treats these separately while peer review groups with C61 (broader significance). Both accept as appropriate context supported by citations.

Strong overlap on discussion claims C62, C64-C66, C69 acknowledging limitations and future directions. Both evaluations support these as appropriately framed speculation. OpenEval treats these as acknowledgment of gaps, peer review as reasonable future directions.
Both address C67 regarding alternative 6mA writers from literature. OpenEval treats separately while peer review groups with broader contextual claims. Both accept as appropriate context.

Extensive overlap on background claims C70-C85, C91-C97. Both evaluations support these as established knowledge providing necessary scientific context. OpenEval covers C70-C97 while peer review covers subset, both without challenge.

Both address C105 (overall novelty claim). OpenEval supports based on totality of evidence and justified novelty given controversial history. Peer review explicitly affirms importance and novelty, with editor and reviewers emphasizing significance of findings.

OpenEval specifically addresses C100 (nuclease treatment controls) as part of DNA localization evidence. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer review R7 covers related DNA localization claims.

OpenEval specifically addresses C102 (functional cooperation between genomics and proteomics data). No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer review R15 broadly affirms the integrated findings.

OpenEval specifically addresses C98 (mass spec as orthogonal method) as part of UPLC-MS/MS evaluation. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer review R8 covers related mass spec claims.

OpenEval specifically addresses C103 (epistasis establishing pathway order) as part of mechanistic evaluation. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer review R11 covers related epistasis claims.

OpenEval specifically addresses C104 (specificity for base damage vs general damage) as part of cell viability evaluation. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer review R13 covers related specificity claims.

OpenEval specifically addresses C4 (KEGG pathway enrichment in DNA repair) as part of screen validation. Peer review R1 covers C1-C3 but does not separately evaluate C4, though it is implicitly accepted.

OpenEval rates therapeutic/clinical implications (C56-C57, C60-C61) as UNCERTAIN, noting they require additional validation. Peer review R18 and R19 cover overlapping claims but rate as SUPPORTED speculation, showing slight difference in evaluation stringency.
